messages.author: 9fec238e3bf8496b
messages.subject: Renjin build problems ( Ubuntu 14.4 )
parts: HI, I’m trying to set up a build environment for Renjin so I can make some modifications, but I can’t get the master branch to build because of test failures in renjin-core. I’ve been through BUILDING.md and followed the directions for Ubuntu 12+, but have had little success. If someone could take a look at my build log and point me in the right direction it would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 3b104dc6686d0c85
messages.subject: Re: Renjin build problems ( Ubuntu 14.4 )
parts:
Adriano,

it looks like you are using a version of GCC that is different from 4.6.x which Renjin needs. If this is correct, please follow the instructions in https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/BUILDING.md to install this particular version of GCC.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan
On Tue, Nov 18, 2014 at 3:24 AM, <adr...@caloiaro.com> wrote:

HI, I’m trying to set up a build environment for Renjin so I can make some modifications, but I can’t get the master branch to build because of test failures in renjin-core. I’ve been through BUILDING.md and followed the directions for Ubuntu 12+, but have had little success. If someone could take a look at my build log and point me in the right direction it would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Renjin build problems ( Ubuntu 14.4 )
parts:
Very strange, it's the same setup I have.

It looks like the problem is actually with Soot, which we use as part of the compilation process after we get GCC's output. 

Can take a look at the tools/gcc-bridge/target/surefire-reports directory and see which file Soot is failing to parse?

-Alex

messages.author: 9fec238e3bf8496b
messages.subject: Re: Renjin build problems ( Ubuntu 14.4 )
parts: Correction: I found the problem in the jimple, but the question is why my system would generate different jimple than yours. The problem is with a cast from long to int on line 117 (and 167). To be more specific, the cast is occurring because the variable in the precious line (116) is being treated as a long rather than an int: T2659 = T2658 * 8L;  . When these casts are removed, the jimple will parse. However, it does introduce a new RuntimeException, presumably because the stack is sized incorrectly as a result of my hand-editing the jimple, yielding the following RuntimeException: StackHeight: -1 from the fill_array function. So the solution lies in the jimple code generation, which I imagine is the product of some decision made farther up the chain; perhaps a decision made by my particular version of gcc when creating the gimple? I’ll take a look farther up the chain.

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Renjin build problems ( Ubuntu 14.4 )
parts:
Ahh, ok, I think understand the problem: GCC is generating gimple with 64 bit pointers, instead of 32 bits. 

GCC-Bridge uses JVM arrays of primitives when a "real" arrays are manipulated with pointer arithmetic and so we are limited to 32-bit indexing. 

Normally, when compiling on a 64 bit system like mine, Renjin will ask GCC to cross-compile to 32-bits with the -m32 argument. But when I look at your maven build log, maven reports that "os.arch=i386"

Is your physical machine 32-bit or 64-bit? Is it possible that you're running a 32-bit JVM on a 64-bit machine? Or are you running a VM to build renjin and Java is getting confused ?

-Alex
